_comment: Per-call timeout CEILING and per-phase BUDGET (seconds) for the engine. wp_timeouts.py resolves both — an exported env var first, then the same key in the skill-root .env (or intel_engine/.env), then this file — and clamps every call to the time left in the active harness phase (HARNESS_PHASE_DEADLINE, epoch seconds, minus phase_deadline_margin) so no call outlives its phase. The call ceiling is exported to child processes; wp_common installs a process-wide urllib.request.urlopen floor at that value and every subprocess runner floors its bound to it. NOT applied to raw DNS/TLS/JARM resolution probes (those keep their short fail-fast bounds by design).

call_timeout._comment: value = the per-call ceiling in seconds (18000 = 5 h; env/.env key CTI_CALL_TIMEOUT). Wrapped as a GROUP on purpose: the RULE-3 loader wp_refs.load_ref only surfaces dict/list nodes, so a bare scalar here is silently ignored and the embedded fallback wins instead.

phase_timeout._comment: value = the wall-clock budget of ONE harness phase in seconds (18000 = 5 h). Env/.env overrides: HARNESS_PHASE_TIMEOUT (orchestrator) and HARNESS_CLI_TIMEOUT (CLI backend), each falling back to the other, then to this value. The CLI backend's MCP tool timeouts (codex tool_timeout_sec, omp mcp.json timeout / OMP_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS) are set from it, so the host never cuts a tool before the phase deadline.

phase_deadline_margin._comment: value = seconds kept in reserve before the phase deadline: a call started inside a phase runs at most min(call ceiling, deadline - now - margin), so it returns a timed-out result while the phase can still record it and move on.

fallback_probe_legs._comment: fallback_probe.py per-leg wall-clock bounds in seconds — each leg runs on its own and a leg that exceeds its bound is reported as {leg: timed_out} while the other legs' findings are returned. Never the call ceiling: one hung archive mirror must not hold the whole probe. archive_is_request bounds each archive.today TimeMap request (two mirrors are tried); kb bounds each local KB subprocess.
